map-empty-put-get-has-length-keys.semantics: functional copy-on-write; first-insertion key order; re-put keeps original position and overwrites value
map-empty-put-get-has-length-keys.notes: keys compared by byte content (Text/Bytes) or value (I64/U64/Bool)

set-empty-add-has-length-to-list.instantiations: sico.set.*[K] with K in {Text,Bytes,Bool,I64,U64}; keys/to_list restricted to K=Text (List[Text] element layout)
set-empty-add-has-length-to-list.semantics: add is idempotent per key; membership and length deterministic

result-option-checked-arithmetic.notes: Result[I64|U64, NumericError] two-slot form; Result[Text|Bytes, NumericError] four-slot form (STEP-0131)

fixed-width-arithmetic.notes: I64/U64 checked_add/checked_sub/checked_mul/checked_div/equal/less_than; checked_div reports division-by-zero (NumericError third case, STEP-0134)

bit-operations.notes: I64/U64 bit_and/bit_or/bit_xor/shl/shr; shift amount shares the operand type and wasm masks counts to [0,63]; shr is arithmetic on I64, logical on U64

http-0-2-0-guest-visible.notes: source-level sico.http2.request (buffered one-shot, Host-default options) emitted beside http@0.1.0; typed http-error surfaces as case-name Text; headers narrowed off the v0 source record; e2e vs TLS fixture server incl. ungranted permission refusal

source-prng-xorshift64.notes: deterministic seeded PRNG as pure Sico source (xorshift64 13/7/17 on U64 bit ops); first 8 outputs of seed 88172645463325252 pinned to a Python reference vector; no ambient randomness

recursion-runtime-bounded.notes: general recursion executable; exhaustion is the typed RunOutcome::StackLimit (resource-limit.stack, exit 125) from the runner wasm-stack budget; the runner stays reusable after exhaustion; payload bindings in all-return matches on computed subjects spill into compiler cells

offline-block-solver-port.notes: 8x8 bitboard solver in pure Sico source (bit ops, general recursion, checked arithmetic); byte-exact vs the frozen Python oracle corpus on trivial/medium/hard/limit fixtures; max_nodes exhaustion yields the typed application-level limit outcome

streaming-transform.notes: bounded-memory stdin/stdout line-numbering transform in pure Sico (4 KiB chunks, 1 MiB driven through default budgets); typed partial failure on non-UTF-8 input; stream reads/writes are host-cancellable

capability-state-machine.notes: fs-persisted sealed/open/burned machine with unary revision guard, typed illegal-transition and stale-refusal outcomes, and deterministic recovery from missing/corrupt documents

string-escapes.notes: source string escapes (\ \n \r \t \0 \") decode to their characters; previously \n silently stayed as two literal characters

source-modules-use.semantics: explicit `module <name>` declaration per imported file (basename must match); `use <module>.<item>` per line; qualified references (module.item); DFS discovery from the entry's use graph in source order; entry file is the program root and declares no module
source-modules-use.notes: imports carry functions only in v0; single-file programs assemble untouched (byte-identical lowering)

packages-user-wit.semantics: `use pkg <name> version <n> expose <Interface>` resolved through `sico-lock.json` (verified signed package, pure component); exposed `interface <Name> version <n>` becomes the `sico:user/<name>@<n>` import identity; qualified `<package>.<function>` calls cross as Component imports; v0 value set per amendment A7 (scalars, one-level lists, Result with scalar error; return area ABI)
packages-user-wit.notes: producer-stamped interface digest (`sico:user-interface` custom section) is the E8016 shape gate; the runner bridges dynamic Val forwarding and re-checks arities fail-closed; no ambient authority for packages

infix-equality-conditions.semantics: infix `left == right` in if conditions lowers to EqualFixed for same-width I64/U64 operands; mixed-width or non-fixed operands keep the typed refusal
infix-equality-conditions.notes: bare integer literals remain unbounded Int (NUM-001 oracle unchanged) — the bare-literal typing decision is recorded as the v1 open question in RFC-0044
